string-array.name: privacy_paragraphs
string-array.item: SCARY has no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no cookies, and there is no SCARY server. Nothing you do in the launcher is sent to us.

Stored only on this TV: your settings and language, pinned and hidden apps, the last 12 movies you opened, your My list, the parental PIN as a salted hash (never the PIN itself), the times of recent crashes (only the time), and cached movie information and images. Uninstalling SCARY or clearing its data in the TV settings deletes all of it. SCARY is excluded from Android backup.
The list of installed apps is read on this TV to show them, and never leaves it.

Also only on this TV: the films you marked \"Loved it\" or \"Not for me\" the day you marked each film as watched, and your bucket list. They power \"Because you loved\", \"How much time do you have?\" and \"Your year in fear\", which are worked out on the TV. The sleep timer is an alarm on the TV that pauses what is playing. The TV\'s own inputs (HDMI, antenna) are read on the TV to show them. The QR code on a film\'s page opens its IMDb page on your phone; the TV sends nothing.

Online movie data, which you can turn off in settings: SCARY asks Cinemeta, the public metadata service of Stremio, for posters, backgrounds, ratings and cast. Only public IMDb movie IDs are sent, plus the search text when you search. Images load from the HTTPS addresses Cinemeta gives, mostly images.metahub.space. Like any website, these services see your TV\'s IP address. The information is cached for 24 hours.

TMDB, only if you enter your own key: requests go to api.themoviedb.org with your key, movie IDs and the interface language. The key is encrypted on this TV with the Android Keystore, is never logged, and is sent only to TMDB. Deleting the key also deletes the TMDB cache. Rent and buy offers on movie pages come from TMDB\'s watch providers (data by JustWatch): the request carries only the movie\'s ID, and your country is picked on the TV from its region setting, or chosen by you in settings, never from your location. If you also sign in to your TMDB account: your session is encrypted on this TV and sent only to TMDB, and SCARY reads your watchlist, favourites and rated films there and sends the horror, thriller and mystery films you add or remove. Signing out deletes the session.
Voice search hands over to this TV\'s own speech recognizer (usually Google). The recording goes to that service, not to SCARY; SCARY only receives the recognized text.

Trailers that play by themselves (on once you agree when first asked; you can turn them off in settings): the player is YouTube\'s, in its privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com, and youtube.com as a last try when a trailer will not play there). When a trailer plays, YouTube (Google) receives your TV\'s IP address, device and browser details and the trailer\'s ID, under Google\'s privacy policy. SCARY blocks cookies in the player and deletes its storage when it closes. No trailer plays offline or in family night.

Phone remote, only while you turn it on in settings: the TV serves a small page on your home network, which your phone opens by scanning a QR code. The code holds a one-time key that signs and encrypts every command between the phone and the TV, and the key is never sent over the network. Commands go straight from the phone to the TV and are not stored; search text and the TMDB key are then used as described above. The page loads nothing from the internet. The remote turns off when you disconnect it, after 30 minutes without use, or when forged commands arrive. To press keys in other apps (Stremio, Netflix…), the phone remote uses SCARY\'s accessibility service, only if you turned it on; it presses keys and reads nothing on the screen.
Watching, trailers and the store open Stremio, YouTube or Google Play. From that point their own privacy policies apply.

Updates (official builds; you can turn the automatic check off in settings): at most every six hours SCARY asks GitHub for the official repository\'s update file. Nothing about you is sent; GitHub sees the TV\'s IP address. An update is downloaded only when you choose \"Update now\", installed only if it is signed with SCARY\'s key, and Android asks you to confirm.

Ask SCARY (AI; off until you agree, once for each service; can be turned off in settings): your question and public facts about the films SCARY offers it to choose from (titles, years, kinds, fear level) go to the AI service you choose: Pollinations (free, no key) or a service with your own key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, DeepSeek, Pollinations, or an address you give). What you watched, your lists and anything that identifies you are never sent; a few words on your taste only if you turn that on. Keys are encrypted on this TV and sent only to their own service. The service sees the TV\'s IP address and its own terms apply; the free service may keep questions and answers. The chat is not saved.
Questions, corrections or requests about your data: d@rubinny.net · github.com/diamondrubinny/Scary/issues
Updated October 2026. This is a draft that has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer.

string-array.name: accessibility_paragraphs
string-array.item: SCARY aims to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA and the Israeli standard IS 5568. It has not yet been audited by an accessibility consultant, so it does not claim full conformance.

Built in: every screen works with the remote\'s arrows and OK button, with a clear focus glow. Cards, buttons and settings have spoken labels for TalkBack, screens and rows have headings, and messages and PIN errors are announced. Holding OK on a poster adds it to My list, and TalkBack offers this as an action. Hebrew and Arabic use a right-to-left layout.

Motion and sound: there is no flashing. The fog and grain are faint and stop when you turn off effects or turn on Remove animations in the TV accessibility settings. Ambient sounds are off by default.

Known limitations: online posters are described only by title and year; the Portuguese, Russian and Arabic translations have not been reviewed by native speakers; very large system font sizes can shorten text in some rows; TalkBack has been tested only on an emulator so far.
Found a barrier? Report it at github.com/diamondrubinny/Scary/issues and describe the screen and what happened. We aim to reply within 14 days.
